## B — Getting Started
Audience: English-language first-time standard-license applicants using the Getting Started section.
Level: beginner study of the selected handbook material, followed by recall and application practice.
Prerequisite policy: understand the cited terminology before comparing exceptions; this is a teaching order, not an extra licensing eligibility requirement.

sections.heading: C — Getting Started
sections.markdown:
## C — Getting Started

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A44
Consult the vehicle owner’s manual for its starting procedure. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A44
In the park-and-drive starting sequence described, begin with the selector in park and apply the brake. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A44
Switch the ignition on to check warning lights and gauges before engaging the engine. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A44
After starting in the described sequence, switch on low-beam headlights and lock the doors. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A44
Before moving forward in drive, check ahead, to the sides and behind, signal, then accelerate gradually. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A44
Operate the accelerator with the front of the foot while keeping the heel on the floor. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A44
The clutch friction point is where the engine and transmission begin engaging as the pedal is released. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A44
As you release a manual clutch, match the vehicle’s forward or reverse movement with accelerator pressure. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A44
To start moving a manual vehicle, hold the brake with the right foot and press the clutch fully down with the left. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A44
Select first gear and release the parking brake before moving off in the manual-start sequence. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A44
Signal the intended direction, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic before moving off. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A44
Ease the clutch to the friction point while looking toward the road rather than at your hands or feet. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A44
Move the right foot from brake to accelerator, add gentle acceleration and finish releasing the clutch slowly. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A44
A forward jerk during a manual start can mean the clutch was released abruptly or too much accelerator was applied. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A44
If the vehicle lurches and stalls during the described manual start, insufficient accelerator input is the stated cause. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A44
Choose gears according to the driving task’s required power and speed; first gear supplies starting power. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A44
The manual gives 15 to 25 miles per hour as a second-gear example, depending on engine power and whether the transmission has 3, 4 or 5 speeds. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A44
Second gear can also be used to start on ice or drive through heavy snow. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A44
For a 3-speed transmission, the manual generally describes third gear for speeds above 25 miles per hour. [A44] [A45]
Source: [A44 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A45
For a small-engine vehicle with a 4- or 5-speed transmission, the third-gear example extends to 30 or 40 miles per hour. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A45
The manual describes fourth gear for driving above 35 miles per hour on a flat road. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A45
Uphill driving may require reaching 40 miles per hour or more before selecting fourth or fifth gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A45
Before an upshift, accelerate to a speed suitable for the intended gear, press the clutch fully down and release the accelerator. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A45
Complete an upshift by selecting the next higher gear, applying accelerator input and progressively releasing the clutch. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A45
Downshifting can provide more power, assist acceleration or steering, and help slow or stop the vehicle. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A45
Downshifting to slow a descent is advised except when the road is slippery. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A45
For a downshift, release the accelerator and use the brake as well if you want to slow. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

Misconceptions: the steering-direction rule also applies in reverse. [A46]
Mnemonic: check, signal, move smoothly, stop smoothly.
Glossary: the friction point is where clutch release begins connecting engine and transmission. [A44]
Dynamic facts: model-specific gear ranges and local idling ordinances need their stated conditions.

sections.heading: C2 — Getting Started
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Getting Started

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A45
Press the clutch fully down and select a lower gear; abrupt deceleration may require skipping to an even lower gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A45
After selecting a lower gear, release the clutch toward its friction point while adding accelerator pressure as needed. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A45
To hold a manual vehicle for an uphill start, set the parking brake, depress the clutch and choose first gear. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A45
For an uphill start, ease the clutch to engagement with gentle acceleration and release the parking brake when the vehicle begins pulling forward. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A45
Continue accelerating in first gear during the uphill start until there is enough speed to shift to second. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A45
Before stopping, check rear traffic in the mirrors, move to the brake and apply smooth, steady pressure. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A45
When stopping a manual vehicle, depress the clutch as the vehicle comes to a halt. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A46
For an unexpected slowdown or stop, quickly tap the brake pedal 3 or 4 times to alert the driver behind. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A46
Turn the steering wheel toward the intended direction in forward travel and in reverse. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A46
Use the 9-and-3 or 8-and-4 hand positions for steering control and reduced airbag-injury risk. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A46
Hold the wheel firmly but gently with the fingers, keeping the thumbs along its face and avoiding a grip on the inside rim. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A46
Check behind the vehicle before entering because small objects and children can be hidden from the driver’s seat. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A46
To begin backing, start the vehicle, apply the brake and select reverse. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A46
For backing, place the left hand at 12 o’clock, rest the right arm behind the passenger seat and look through the rear window. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A46
Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera when reversing; each leaves part of the rear area unseen. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A46
Back no faster than a slow walking pace and steer toward the intended movement of the vehicle’s rear. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A46
When turning in reverse, make brief checks ahead and to the sides while continuing to look rearward until fully stopped. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A46
Minimize backing and avoid reversing into traffic. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A46
Back into a driveway or parking space unless signs prohibit it so you can leave facing forward. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A47
The handbook advises limiting idling around a start or stop to 1 minute. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A47
Gentle driving during the first few minutes warms the engine more efficiently than extended idling. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A47
Idling wastes fuel and releases harmful pollutants. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A47
Some Maine local governments have ordinances restricting idling. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]
